## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified (source trace):** the fix closes the stale-fallback crash path described in #12330, and no regression was found in the reviewed scope. The ordinary path, where at least one sink or source is available, returns the same array as before. Only the fallback branch changes.

Traced through Quickshell v0.3.1 and Qt 6.11.2:

```text
node removed (registry removal, or full reset on client reconnect)
  -> PwNodeIface deleted: existing QML wrappers go null first,
     then Pipewire.nodes.values drops the interface in QObject::destroyed
  -> rawAudioSinks / rawAudioSources empty
  -> fallback branch taken on the next 75 ms refresh or on panel open

  base:  cachedAudioSinks unfiltered -> Repeater model QVariantList
         -> dead wrapper becomes a typed-null QObject*
         -> required-property delegate (SinkRow) builds its dynamic metaobject
         -> QQmlDMListAccessorData::createMissingProperties dereferences it (no null check)
  head:  Model.livingNodes(cachedAudioSinks, nodes)
         -> identity match against the live list, which never holds a destroyed interface
         -> [] or only live cached nodes; no delegate is built from a destroyed node
```

**Verified (trigger coverage, source only):** the WirePlumber kill or crash trigger and the later single-ALSA-error trigger in #12330 both reach this same fallback. In the second case, Quickshell's client reconnect resets the registry and destroys every node without any daemon restarting. Opening the panel after a teardown also snapshots the fallback directly, so the filter covers that path as well.

Mapping the unsymbolized frames in the issue (`libQt6QmlModels.so.6+0xb3530`) to `createMissingProperties` fits the traced path but was not confirmed with symbols or a native run.

### Code comment overstates what `PwObjectTracker` does

The new comment in `Panel.qml` (and the PR description) says nothing keeps the cached nodes alive because "the PwObjectTracker below tracks candidateSinks, not the cache". That implies tracking the cache would keep them alive. In Quickshell v0.3.1, `PwObjectTracker` only binds and unbinds the node proxy; the registry deletes the node regardless.

**Impact:** a future reader could "fix" this by adding the cache to a `PwObjectTracker`, which would not prevent the crash.

**Suggested change:** describe the actual cause instead, for example: "The registry destroys these nodes regardless of PwObjectTracker; the cache still holds their JS wrappers, which Qt turns into null QObject* model entries that crash required-property delegates."

**Optional test improvement:** the four new `livingNodes` assertions use `assertDeepEqual`, which compares through JSON serialization, and the live and dropped fixtures have different `name` values. An implementation that matched by `name` instead of identity would therefore pass all four (established by reading `test/shell.d/base-test.sh`, not by running it). A case with a distinct object sharing a live node's `name`, expected to be dropped, would pin the identity behavior the helper's comment describes.
